sections.html: Beckham County is in southwestern Oklahoma, with Sayre as county seat. The 2020 population was 22,411, including 11,566 in Elk City, which sits 18 miles northeast of Sayre. The other incorporated towns are Carter, Erick, Sweetwater and Texola. Farming and livestock have long anchored the local economy, and oil has had its boom and bust years. Much of the housing stock is older houses, rural parcels and inherited property, so tax records on those homes deserve a look before you list.

Property tax is split between two Sayre offices, and which one you call depends on the question.

  • Assessor, 301 E Main St. #2, Sayre, OK 73662, (580) 928-3329: why your value is what it is.
  • Treasurer, (580) 928-2589 or Treasurer@beckhamcountyok.gov, mail to P.O. Box 600, Sayre, OK 73662: what you owe and when.

The Assessor does not set rates, write budgets or collect money. Rates come from the local taxing jurisdictions, and the Assessor's website offers a property tax estimator and a school district mill rate lookup. The Treasurer collects and divides all ad valorem tax among the county and its subdivisions, and pursues delinquent accounts through tax sales.

sections.h2: Due dates, penalties and how to pay
sections.html:
Bills come due November 1. Pay everything, or just the first half, by December 31, and the second half by March 31. Any statement of $25 or less has to be paid in one payment.

Beckham County property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
March 15Assessor deadline for homestead and other exemptions and for personal property renditions without penalty
October 1Assessor certifies the tax amounts to be collected
November 1Taxes first become due
Mid-NovemberCurrent statements are mailed
December 31Last day for full payment or first half before delinquency
March 31Last day for the second half
Second Monday in JuneTax resale at the Treasurer's office, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.

After December 31 a penalty of 1.5 percent per month builds up, and the second half begins to accrue in April. A statement that never reaches you is no defense (O.S. 68 section 2915). Homes with an escrow account get their statement at the lender, which often sends payment in late December, so posting may slip into early January.

Online payment runs through the Treasurer's tax roll page, where a third party adds $1.75 for an eCheck or 2.95 percent of the tax for a card. In person, the courthouse lobby has a drop box at the security desk.

sections.h2: From market value to your bill
sections.html:
The Assessor starts with market value, found through recognized appraisal methods, and multiplies by the state's assessment ratio to get assessed value. Exemptions are subtracted to produce taxable value, and millage is applied to that last number.

Several things feed the estimate:

  • Recent sales and market activity in the area.
  • Size, age, quality and condition of the house.
  • Location and neighborhood influences.
  • Construction type, additions and new building.
  • Comparable properties.

Oklahoma restrains yearly growth in taxable market value to 3 percent for farmland or a home with a homestead exemption, and 5 percent for everything else. A sale or transfer wipes the restraint out. That is why a buyer can inherit a noticeably bigger value than the seller ever paid on.

A protest has to be written, and the Assessor must receive it inside 30 days of the Change of Value Notice mailing. No notice at all? You have until the first Monday in April. On Form 974, the informal protest, state what you think the house is worth and attach evidence such as a sale, comparables or an appraisal.

Let the 30 days slip and the Assessor's number is final for that year. File on time and you get an informal hearing, held by phone or face to face. If that fails, Form 976 takes the dispute to the county board of equalization, and everything wraps up by May 31 or whenever the board adjourns.

Photographs, measurements, sales data and correction details all help. Skip the appeal if closing is days away, but do not ignore a real error, because it will keep following the house.

Homestead status trims $1,000 from the assessed valuation of the home you live in. You qualify as an Oklahoma resident occupying the house by January 1. Bring the application to the Assessor's office or mail Form OTC 921 before March 15 each year.

You do not re-file annually as long as you remain and the deed is unchanged. Your buyer starts fresh with their own application. In-person help sessions for exemptions and personal property exist too, so ask the Assessor when the next one is.

Deeds above $100 owe documentary stamp tax at $0.75 for each $500 of consideration, minus any liens left on the property. Stamps are purchased from the county clerk at filing. Print the buyer's complete address on the deed. Claiming an exemption means writing the statute reference on it. The clerk can confirm the current rate.

The mortgage tax is its own charge. It falls on a mortgage and never on an ordinary deed. It runs from 2 cents to 10 cents per $100 by term, plus a $10.00 certification fee per mortgage. If your buyer pays cash, none of it applies.

sections.h2: Before you list a Beckham County house
sections.html:
Gather a few papers before the first showing: the latest Change of Value Notice, the newest tax statement, and a note of which half is still unpaid. Check with the Assessor that the homestead exemption is in your name, and ask the Treasurer if the account has a balance. Buyers in Elk City and Sayre alike will want the same few answers: what the taxable value is, what the last bill was, and whether the account is clear.

Inherited the house? Get the deed into the correct name before listing. The tax offices cannot update an account until the transfer is recorded, so an outdated name sends statements to the wrong person. A farm or acreage parcel may also carry agricultural limits on value growth, which a buyer using the land differently should ask about.

The county can put delinquent property up at the June resale once it has held the tax lien for two full years. Before then, the balance usually comes out of your sale proceeds. Request a payoff from the Treasurer before signing a contract.

  1. Call the Treasurer at (580) 928-2589 for the payoff.
  2. Confirm that your homestead exemption is on file with the Assessor.
  3. Hand the payoff to the title company so it is settled at closing.

A cash buyer can close over a tax balance, which helps when a house has fallen behind. The calendar above covers every seller in the county, town or farm.

faqs.q: What dates matter for a Beckham County tax bill?
faqs.a: Bills are due November 1. The full amount or first half is safe through December 31, and the second half through March 31. Small statements of $25 or less go in one payment.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost in Beckham County?
faqs.a: Interest-style penalty of 1.5 percent a month starts after December 31 and runs until you pay. For the second half it starts in April.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Beckham County valuation protest?
faqs.a: To the Assessor, in writing, on Form 974. The clock is 30 days from the mailing date of your Change of Value Notice, or the first Monday in April if no notice came.

faqs.q: What does the homestead exemption save in Beckham County?
faqs.a: It lowers the assessed valuation of your primary residence by $1,000. Live in the house by January 1 and apply by March 15.

faqs.q: Does unpaid tax block a sale in Beckham County?
faqs.a: No. The balance is normally cleared from the proceeds at closing, and a cash buyer can close with it still open. Ask the Treasurer for the payoff first.
